::: {#lem-parent-edge}
#### Every edge joins a vertex to its parent

Let $T$ be a rooted tree (@def-rooted-tree).
For every edge $\set{u, w}$ of $T$, one of $u$ and $w$ is the parent (@def-tree-parent) of the other.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $r$ be the root, and let $r = p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_m = u$ be the path from $r$ to $u$ (@thm-tree-paths).
Also $w \ne u$, since a tree has no loops (@rem-tree-simple).

- If $w$ is not on this path, then $p_0, \ldots, p_m, w$ is a path from $r$ to $w$,
  since its vertices are all different and $\set{u, w}$ is an edge.
  By @thm-tree-paths it is the path from $r$ to $w$, so $u$ is the parent of $w$.
- If $w$ is on this path, then $w = p_i$ for some $i < m$.
  If $i = m - 1$, then $w$ is the parent of $u$.
  Suppose, for contradiction (@def-proof-by-contradiction), that $i \le m - 2$.
  Then $p_i, p_{i + 1}, \ldots, p_m, p_i$, whose last step uses the edge $\set{u, w}$,
  is a closed walk of length $m - i + 1 \ge 3$
  whose vertices before the last one are all different.
  As in the proof of @thm-tree-paths, its edges are all different,
  so it is a cycle (@def-graph-cycle), which a tree does not have.

:::

:::
